answer: A new identity gains voting and grading rights only after one full epoch as intern to a randomly assigned mentor, and each mentor may take only one intern at a time. The mentor locks timber from spendable balance as a performance bond; the intern has only sparrow rights to answer and attest. If clustering or shared-key evidence later ties the intern to a farm, the bond and the intern's remaining ember of unvested rewards are slashed. Forging N influential identities therefore needs N mentors, N locked bonds, and N sequential epochs—cost and delay that cannot be parallelized cheaply.
